content: Your doctor has determined that the benefits of using this medication outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States or Canada and experience side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. Precautions: Before taking quinine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, quinidine, or mefloquine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other complications. This medication may cause dizziness or blurred vision. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Limit your intake of alcoholic beverages. Quinine may lead to a condition affecting heart rhythm known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also heighten this risk. This may occur if you are using certain drugs (e.g., diuretics or water pills) or have conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Discuss the risks, benefits, and treatment options with your doctor. Quinine passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm most nursing infants. Your doctor may test your infant for a specific enzyme deficiency (glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency, or G6PD) before you breastfeed. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications can affect the removal of quinine from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Similarly, quinine can slow the removal of other medications from your body, which may affect how they work. Many drugs, including amiodarone, dofetilide, mefloquine, pimozide, procainamide, quinidine, sotalol, and macrolide antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin), can also affect heart rhythm (QT prolongation). Quinine is very similar to quinidine. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., urine tests for catecholamines, protein, or steroids), potentially causing false test results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Monitoring: While taking this medication, your doctor may order laboratory and/or medical tests, such as G6PD blood levels, vision tests, blood potassium levels, liver/kidney function tests, and EKGs, to monitor your condition and check for side effects. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is more than 4 hours after the missed dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
